reason: While the text establishes the Israelites (בְנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל) as a distinct nation clearly separated from the Egyptians, it does not portray them as possessing or having their own specific land. The passage focuses on their exodus FROM Egypt (departure from Rameses toward Sukkot) rather than arrival at or possession of their own territory. The narrative emphasizes their liberation and establishment as a distinct people, but does not depict them as a nation with territorial holdings of their own.
